summary: CI-only change. Every cached jdx/mise-action step in 12 workflows gains `cache_key_prefix: mise-v1-<ubuntu image>` matching its job's runs-on, so jobs on blacksmith ubuntu-2204 (glibc 2.35) and ubuntu-2404 (glibc 2.39) no longer share one mise cache entry holding source-built cargo tools. A new vitest guard (run by tests.yml's lint job via `pnpm run test:scripts`) enforces the rule for every workflow and limits composite actions to image-independent tools. An independent re-implementation of the guard over all workflows at head found all 29 cached steps keyed to the correct image and every publish/release path still `cache: false`. No shipped artefact, library code or release workflow is altered. Residual risk is low: the change relies on both pinned mise-action versions (v3.6.3 and v4) honouring `cache_key_prefix`, which could not be checked offline, and the first run after merge will be a cold cache for every job.

behaviour_changes.description: Cached mise-action steps now restore/save under an image-specific key prefix (mise-v1-ubuntu-2204 or mise-v1-ubuntu-2404) instead of mise-action's default prefix, separating cache entries between runner images with different glibc versions.

New discovery test scripts/__tests__/workflow-mise-cache-image.test.mjs fails CI if any cached mise step lacks the image prefix matching runs-on, sets cache_key, sets a prefix with caching off, or if a composite action caches non-image-independent tools.

All existing mise cache entries become unreachable for workflow steps (new keys), so each job cold-installs its mise toolset, including source-built cargo tools, on the first run per key/scope after merge.

failure_scenarios.title: Pinned mise-action version ignores cache_key_prefix, so the guard passes while the shared key remains
failure_scenarios.trigger: A pinned mise-action revision (v3.6.3 at 5228313e, or v4 at 1648a781) does not declare or honour the cache_key_prefix input.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: GitHub Actions only warns on an undeclared `with:` input. The new test checks the YAML statically (E-2) and cannot tell whether the action uses the value, so an ignored input would leave the default distro-agnostic key in place with a green check.
failure_scenarios.consequence: The GLIBC_2.38 cross-image cache poisoning the change targets could recur on the next mise config change: CI jobs fail before tests run. No shipped artefact is affected; a loud CI failure, not a silent one.

existing_verification.description: Static guard asserting the prefix is set per runs-on image.

missing_verification: Confirmation, from the action's action.yml at each pinned SHA or from a CI log line showing the restored key, that cache_key_prefix is honoured.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: On the PR's CI run, check a mise-action step log for a cache key starting `mise-v1-ubuntu-2204`/`mise-v1-ubuntu-2404` for one v3.6.3 job (tests-rust) and one v4 job (tests-crates).

failure_scenarios.title: Cold mise caches after merge slow every job and may hit job timeouts
failure_scenarios.trigger: First run of each workflow on main and on each PR branch after merge, before the new keys are saved.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: New prefixes mean no existing entry matches; jobs install the whole mise toolset, including cargo: tools that build from source (E-11), uncached.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Longer CI runs and runner cost; a job with a tight timeout-minutes could fail once. Self-heals once each key is saved.
missing_verification: CI timings for the PR run were not available.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Accept a one-off slow run; re-run any timed-out job once the cache is populated.
